label: context.reference
description: Arrange event-driven work by inspecting its condition, receiving task and result path.
text:
Use this guide for work that should happen later, repeatedly or in response to an event. Establish the intended action, the condition that should start it and where the result belongs. Use the existing conversation and ask only about ambiguity that would change the outcome.

Inspect relevant existing triggers and the interfaces available in this installation. A time schedule, an incoming message, changed data or another event may need different owners. Reuse an arrangement that fits. When it does not, inspect the current contract and source of the relevant owner and adapt or implement the capability within your grant.

Trace the condition through to its consumer. Find the receiving run, the provider or tool that performs the work, and the route that delivers the result. Look for related inputs, outputs, retained state or future templates that must change together. The task-authoring guide describes provider frontier ownership; other owners define their own contracts. Copying a few visible checkpoints does not establish the complete connection.

Choose verification from the behavior and remaining uncertainty. Read back an edit when that establishes the changed configuration; inspect the owner or receiving route when acceptance is in question. For timing, confirm the intended timezone, repetition and next due condition using the installed interface. A clean preview covers its reported checks. Execution and delivery require their own evidence when they are part of the claimed result. Do not fire an external action solely to test the setup.

Explain what will happen, under what condition and where the result will appear. If it is armed but has not fired, say that. Save a reusable procedure only with the limits of what was actually demonstrated, so another run can adapt it to its own installation.
